title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed page numbered '45bis'. It is an insert, marked with a circled ×, meant to go into p.45, and ends with a pointer '→ ⊗⊗ p.45'. Grothendieck's handwritten page number '11' sits at the bottom. The neighbouring folder pages are handwritten p-adic computations: Legendre's formula v_p(n!) = (n − sum of digits)/(p−1), and the condition v_p(π) ≥ 1/(p−1) for π^n/n! to stay integral, with strict inequality for v_p(π^n/n!) → ∞, i.e. divided powers on (π). That pattern suggests Grothendieck used the back of a typed manuscript, probably one received or circulated (the folder mentions a letter of 1965), as scratch paper. The typed text itself is not about crystals.

The mathematics belongs to the theory of local heights on an abelian variety A over a field K with absolute values v, in the style of Néron's quasi-functions or Lang's and Tate's local height functions.
- q is some data defined over K; it may be a quadratic or divisor-type datum.
- a and its approximations a_m give objects ξ_0(q_{a_m}). These are local symbols or quasi-functions evaluated on the degree-zero cycle (x) − (0) at the place v.
- μ(q,a) is defined as the limit as m → ∞. This is the familiar Tate-type limit construction of a canonical local height.

The claim in item (v) is a rationality, or 'defined over K', statement:
1. If a is rational over K and q is defined over K, then each ξ_0(q_{a_m}) is defined over K.
2. Concretely, for x ∈ A(L) with L/K finite, the value at ((x) − (0), v) depends only on the restriction w of v to L.
3. Since this holds for every m, it passes to the limit.
4. Hence μ(q,a)((x) − (0), v) also depends only on w, which is the meaning of 'μ(q,a) is defined over K'.

This is a standard functoriality and descent step for local height pairings.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The argument is a straightforward passage to the limit, assuming convergence for each fixed (x, v), which was presumably established earlier in the manuscript.
Typo in the typescript: 'infimi' should be 'infini'.

ideas.what: Field-of-definition (dependence only on the restriction of v to L) of local height-type symbols ξ_0(q_{a_m}) and of their limit μ(q,a)
ideas.modern_name: Rationality / Galois-invariance of Néron local height functions (canonical local heights) defined by a limit construction
ideas.usually_credited_to: A. Néron (quasi-fonctions et hauteurs, 1965); J. Tate's limit construction; S. Lang
ideas.where_published: Néron, Ann. of Math. 82 (1965); Lang, Fundamentals of Diophantine Geometry

deep.surprise_reason: The typed page appears to be part of someone else's manuscript on local heights, perhaps related to Néron's work, used as a support sheet. It contains a routine descent-by-limit argument. The adjacent handwritten p-adic divided-power computations are classical. A thematic link between heights and crystalline work is coincidental rather than a missed connection.
transcription_corrections: The heavily struck-out word before 'la limite' is illegible; '[-l'infini[?]-]' is a guess, and the typed text actually reads 'Par passage à ... la limite pour m infimi' (typo for 'infini').
'qu'il en: est' is 'qu'il en est' with an overstrike.
The final handwritten note reads '→ (xx) p.45', a circled double cross referring back to p.45. The opening mark is a circled single ×, not ⊗.
